001package armyc2.c2sd.renderer.utilities;
002
003public interface IMultiPointRenderer {
004
005    /**
006     * Renders all multi-point symbols, creating KML that can be used to draw
007     * it on a Google map.  Multipoint symbols cannot be draw the same 
008     * at different scales. For instance, graphics with arrow heads will need to 
009     * redraw arrowheads when you zoom in on it.  Similarly, graphics like a 
010     * Forward Line of Troops drawn with half circles can improve performance if 
011     * clipped when the parts of the graphic that aren't on the screen.  To help 
012     * readjust graphics and increase performance, this function requires the 
013     * scale and bounding box to help calculate the new locations.
014     * @param id A unique identifier used to identify the symbol by Google map. 
015     * The id will be the folder name that contains the graphic.
016     * @param name a string used to display to the user as the name of the 
017     * graphic being created.
018     * @param description a brief description about the graphic being made and 
019     * what it represents.
020     * @param symbolCode A 15 character symbolID corresponding to one of the
021     * graphics in the MIL-STD-2525C
022     * @param controlPoints The vertices of the graphics that make up the
023     * graphic.  Passed in the format of a string, using decimal degrees 
024     * separating lat and lon by a comma, separating coordinates by a space.  
025     * The following format shall be used "x1,y1[,z1] [xn,yn[,zn]]..."
026     * @param altitudeMode Indicates whether the symbol should interpret 
027     * altitudes as above sea level or above ground level. Options are 
028     * "clampToGround", "relativeToGround" (from surface of earth), "absolute" 
029     * (sea level), "relativeToSeaFloor" (from the bottom of major bodies of 
030     * water).
031     * @param scale A number corresponding to how many meters one meter of our 
032     * map represents. A value "50000" would mean 1:50K which means for every 
033     * meter of our map it represents 50000 meters of real world distance.
034     * @param bbox The viewable area of the map.  Passed in the format of a
035     * string "lowerLeftX,lowerLeftY,upperRightX,upperRightY." Not required
036     * but can speed up rendering in some cases.
037     * example: "-50.4,23.6,-42.2,24.2"
038     * @param modifiers A JSON string representing all the possible symbol 
039     * modifiers represented in the MIL-STD-2525C.  Format of the string will be
040     * {"modifiers": {"attributeName":"value"[,"attributeNamen":"valuen"]...}}
041     * The quotes are literal in the above notation.  Example: 
042     * {"modifiers": {"quantity":"4","speed":"300","azimuth":[100,200]}}
043     * @param format An enumeration: 0 for KML, 1 for JSON.
044     * @param symStd An enumeration: 0 for 2525Bch2, 1 for 2525C.
045     * @return A JSON string representation of the graphic.
046     */
047    public String RenderSymbol(String id, String name, String description, 
048            String symbolCode, String controlPoints, String altitudeMode,
049            double scale, String bbox, String modifiers, int format, int symStd);
050    
051    
052    /**
053     * Renders all multi-point symbols, creating KML or JSON for the user to
054     * parse and render as they like.
055     * This function requires the bounding box to help calculate the new
056     * locations.
057     * @param id A unique identifier used to identify the symbol by Google map.
058     * The id will be the folder name that contains the graphic.
059     * @param name a string used to display to the user as the name of the 
060     * graphic being created.
061     * @param description a brief description about the graphic being made and 
062     * what it represents.
063     * @param symbolCode A 15 character symbolID corresponding to one of the
064     * graphics in the MIL-STD-2525C
065     * @param controlPoints The vertices of the graphics that make up the
066     * graphic.  Passed in the format of a string, using decimal degrees
067     * separating lat and lon by a comma, separating coordinates by a space.
068     * The following format shall be used "x1,y1 [xn,yn]..."
069     * @param pixelWidth pixel dimensions of the viewable map area
070     * @param pixelHeight pixel dimensions of the viewable map area
071     * @param bbox The viewable area of the map.  Passed in the format of a
072     * string "lowerLeftX,lowerLeftY,upperRightX,upperRightY."
073     * example: "-50.4,23.6,-42.2,24.2"
074     * @param symbolModifiers A JSON string representing all the possible symbol
075     * modifiers represented in the MIL-STD-2525C.  Format of the string will be
076     * {"modifiers": {"attributeName":"value"[,"attributeNamen":"valuen"]...}}
077     * The quotes are literal in the above notation.  Example:
078     * {"modifiers": {"quantity":"4","speed":"300","azimuth":[100,200]}}
079     * @param format An enumeration: 0 for KML, 1 for JSON.
080     * @param symStd An enumeration: 0 for 2525Bch2, 1 for 2525C.
081     * @return A JSON (1) or KML (0) string representation of the graphic.
082     */
083    public String RenderSymbol2D(String id, String name, String description, String symbolCode, String controlPoints,
084            int pixelWidth, int pixelHeight, String bbox, String modifiers, int format, int symStd);
085        
086}
